title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama / Mistral / Qwen (GQA/MQA kernel & scheduler tuning)
author: Arjun Patel
description: Motivation: our generic kernel and scheduling heuristics produce suboptimal performance for several recently onboarded models (Llama variants, Mistral, Qwen) where memory layout and attention patterns interact with GQA/MQA quantization modes. This PR introduces targeted model-specific heuristics and runtime fallbacks: 1) kernel selection: prefer fused attention kernels for Qwen/GQA when sequence length < 1024 and use MQA-friendly matmul paths for Llama variants when KFLOP utilization falls below threshold, 2) scheduler: add a lightweight per-model priority tier and time-sliced continuous-batching window to reduce p99 latency spikes for short requests, 3) KV cache: prefetch alignment for Mistral large-context models and compact metadata encoding to lower cache lookup overhead, 4) quantization-path tuning: automatic selection between GQA and MQA backends based on sequence-length histogram and attention head parity, plus a dynamic fallback to fp16 kernels if quality regresses. Implementation notes: changes are feature-gated behind a runtime flag (runtime.model_heuristics.v2) and exercised under perf-canary and unit tests; default behavior unchanged until rollout. Benchmarks: internal microbench on dedicated clusters shows ~18-23% p99 latency reduction for Llama 13B inference at batch=1, 12-16% throughput improvement for Mistral-7B across mixed-length workloads, and ~10-14% token-cost reduction for Qwen-14B in GQA mode due to better kernel selection and reduced kernel launch overhead. Safety: added regression guards (output-diff thresholds and eval prompt set) to detect quality regressions; fallback path included. Rollout: canary to 5% of traffic for 48h, metrics monitored in Console dashboards (latency by model, output-similarity, request-failure-rate). Related: ENG-10234 (kernel selection), ENG-10267 (continuous batching), SUP-445 (customer-reported Qwen latency regression).
